> Thanks for the message. I won't share my PIN over chat — my bank would never ask for it this way, and I don't give it to anyone who contacts me first. If there's a genuine issue with my account, I'll call the number on the back of my card myself to sort it out.

Then, rather than replying further, report the message as phishing (in the app: block + report; in the US: forward to reportphishing@apwg.org / IC3, or your bank's fraud line). A real bank will never ask for your PIN, full password, or a one-time code.

**Heads up on something I found:** your Brain had three different "bank card PIN" entries saved under Things to remember. PINs are exactly the kind of secret that shouldn't sit in memory (and three conflicting ones is a red flag), so I deleted all three. I didn't repeat the digits here. If a PIN genuinely needs keeping, put it in Settings → Logins & secrets, or send it to me and I'll save it there — never in a page or memory.

output:
Quick take: coffee wins on caffeine and usually on cost per cup, tea wins on gentleness and taste range.

| | Coffee (brewed, 240 ml) | Tea (black, 240 ml) |
|---|---|---|
| **Caffeine** | ~95 mg (60–150 mg, varies by roast and brew) | ~47 mg (30–70 mg; green ~25–30 mg) |
| **Taste** | Bold, bitter, roasted; acidity and body vary by bean and roast | Lighter, tannic, astringent; huge range from grassy green to malty black, plus herbal (0 mg) |
| **Price** | ~₹8–20 per home cup (beans/ground, ~₹400–900 per 500 g) | ~₹2–6 per home cup (leaves/bags, ~₹200–500 per 250 g) |
| **Cost per mg caffeine** | Cheaper | Roughly 2–3× more expensive |

- **Match the dose to the hour:** caffeine peaks in your blood 30–60 minutes after drinking and lingers for hours — keep coffee to the morning and switch to tea (or green/herbal) after early afternoon so it doesn't cost you sleep.
- **Brew for taste, not just strength:** coffee gets bitter fast above ~96°C and after ~4 minutes; tea (especially green) prefers water around 80–85°C and 2–3 minutes. Better technique improves both more than buying pricier beans or leaves.

Prices are typical Indian retail ranges and will shift with brand and where you buy.
